clue.text: Bit of coffee offered by European, tall figure

parts.note: a coffee bean is one small piece of coffee
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: Someone tall is handed a coffee bean by a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of coffee' looks like a sip; it is a single bean. A beanpole is a very tall thin person.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal term for a very tall, thin person, likened to the long stake for climbing beans.

clue.text: Rowdy film stars having part to play in rear

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit inside the word for the rear

parts.note: the rear or back of something

indicators.note: letters given room to play are free to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Unruly actors get a role to perform at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rowdy' belongs to the definition, not an anagram signal: the Brat Pack were young actors known for wild behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickname given in the 1980s to a group of young, often badly behaved Hollywood actors.

clue.text: Take over training with fuss at the front

indicators.note: the fuss is placed ahead of the training in the answer

parts.note: ado is a fuss or bother
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: Someone assumes control of a training session with a lot of fuss up front.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt an idea or a child is to take it on as your own.

clue.text: Fight with drink on the increase?

parts.note: punch is a mixed drink served from a bowl
up means rising or increasing

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out as drinking goes up.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for a brawl with fists.

clue.text: Landed Scotsman, cut off retreat

indicators.note: the landowner's title loses its tail letter

parts.note: a laird is a Scottish landowner

explanation.surface: A Scottish landowner is cut off from his hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut off' removes the last letter, D, from LAIRD.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's den is its retreat or hiding place.

clue.text: 'Sun' involved in junk communication before news, finally, in brief spurts

indicators.note: the sun's letter is wrapped up inside the junk mail

parts.note: spam is unwanted junk email

indicators.note: the closing letter of the word news is taken

explanation.surface: A tabloid gets caught up in junk mail ahead of the news, in short bursts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' looks like the newspaper; it is just S. 'before' puts the last letter of news after SPASM.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasms are sudden short bursts of activity or muscular contraction.

clue.text: Show retired brother familiar saying

parts.note: to prove is to show something is true

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, so the brother's abbreviation goes backwards

explanation.surface: A retired brother demonstrates a well-known saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb is a well-known short saying giving advice.

clue.text: Tiny mark on potato picked up for one in stand?

indicators.note: picked up as by the ear, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: a speck is a tiny mark and tater is slang for potato

explanation.surface: A small blemish on a spud gets noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: SPECK TATER, said aloud, gives the answer. 'Stand' is the grandstand at a sports ground, not something to stand on.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator watches from the stands at a sports ground.

clue.text: Leading companion showing formality

parts.note: a star plays the leading role
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A principal partner displays a stiff manner.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the post-nominal for Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch figuratively means stiffness or formality of manner.

clue.text: A connection around university that's widely evident

indicators.note: the connection is wrapped around the university's letter

parts.note: bonding is making a connection

explanation.surface: A link around a university is plain for all to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abounding is plentiful and found everywhere.

clue.text: Greet effusively good boy with promise of marriage

parts.note: a lad is a boy
to give one's hand is to promise marriage

explanation.surface: A nice young man proposes and greets her warmly.
explanation.definitionFit: To glad-hand is to greet people with exaggerated warmth, as a politician does.

clue.text: Musical work stocked in shop eradicated

indicators.note: the answer is carried in the shop's words as stock is kept on shelves

explanation.surface: A piece of music is wiped from the shop's shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a dramatic work set to music.

clue.text: Like something sewn on uniform? No

definitions.meaning: resembling a cloth piece stitched on

explanation.definitionFit: Patchy means both made of sewn-on pieces and uneven or inconsistent.

clue.text: Sublime speaker's device to include a quip

indicators.note: the microphone holds the other letters within it

parts.note: a mic is a microphone used by a speaker
a jest is a quip or joke

explanation.surface: A public speaker's microphone takes in a witty line, a grand effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Majestic means having grandeur, as does sublime.

clue.text: Start of strategy to withdraw surveillance

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word strategy

parts.note: to take out is to withdraw, as money from a bank

explanation.surface: The beginning of a plan to pull out of a watch operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake-out is a period of secret police watch on a place.

clue.text: Top sportsman with time in heat set off scrap to show impatience

parts.note: a champ is a champion

indicators.note: the time letter goes inside the rearranged letters
set off means jumbled, so the letters of heat are rearranged

parts.note: a bit is a scrap or small piece

explanation.surface: A champion athlete, starting his heat on time, gets in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' rearranges HEAT into ATHE, and 'in' puts T inside it to make ATTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from a horse biting its bit, meaning to be eager and restless to start.

clue.text: Aggressive type having trouble in a ship with colonist

parts.note: SS is a steamship
to ail is to trouble
an ant lives in a colony

explanation.surface: An attacker comes across difficulties on board a ship with a settler.
explanation.walkthrough: An ant counts as a colonist because ants live in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is an attacker, so someone aggressive.

clue.text: Brainy barrister discontented when tucking into breakfast dish

indicators.note: the pair of letters gets placed inside the breakfast dish

parts.note: cereal is eaten at breakfast

indicators.note: with its contents gone only the outer letters of barrister are left

explanation.surface: An unhappy lawyer digs into his morning bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' means emptied of its contents, leaving only the outside letters; 'tucking into' sounds like eating but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebral means intellectual, appealing to the brain.

clue.text: Nominal candidate rethinks goals when upset

indicators.note: the letters, once upset, are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A token candidate reconsiders their aims after being upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalking horse is a candidate put up to test or hide a stronger contender.

clue.text: Speech giving notice to groom?

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
to dress is to groom, as a horse or hair

explanation.surface: A notice being given to a bridegroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' looks like the bridegroom; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal speech.

clue.text: Wine? A small measure's included in resting place

indicators.note: the letters are placed inside the wine

parts.note: hock is German white wine
mm is a millimetre, a small measure; 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A glass of wine, a modest measure, where one lies back.
explanation.walkthrough: HOCK is a British name for a German white wine from the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: A hammock is a hanging bed for resting.

clue.text: Cave is reached around end of tour

indicators.note: the reached phrase is placed around the letter

parts.note: a place one got to is one that is reached

indicators.note: the final letter of the word tour

explanation.surface: A cavern is arrived at as the tour finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small picturesque cave.

clue.text: One plays a small part in a downfall?

definitions.text: One plays a small part in a downfall?

parts.words: One plays a small part in a downfall?
parts.note: a downfall is read as a fall of rain, of which one drop is a tiny part

explanation.definitionFit: A single drop of water that makes up a shower of rain.

clue.text: Burden young offender with some medicine? Not at first

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: the opening letter of the medicine is left out

parts.note: a dose is an amount of medicine

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster is loaded with medicine, though not at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not at first' drops D from DOSE, leaving OSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To impose is to place a burden on someone.

clue.text: Stink created by party in time? That's not hard

indicators.note: the following letter is left out of the result
the party is placed inside the time

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time
a do is a party
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A smell arises at a party at some hour, though not a strong one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not hard' removes the H for hard, as pencils are graded, from the combined letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a smell, often an unpleasant one.

clue.text: A short drink held up in Italian city

indicators.note: in a down entry, held up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sip is a small drink

explanation.surface: A quick drink is raised in a town in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisa is a city in Tuscany, famous for its leaning tower.

clue.text: Follow tense athletics event

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a race is a track event

explanation.surface: Watch a nervy track event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like nervous; it is the grammatical term.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace is to follow a path or track someone down.

clue.text: Standard often found flying abroad?

parts.note: a standard is a flag, and three-banded flags fly in many foreign countries

explanation.definitionFit: A flag of three colours in bands, like those of France or Italy.

clue.text: Dull-witted baronet falls in river

indicators.note: the baronet drops inside the river

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A slow nobleman tumbles into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The OUSE is a river in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow to understand.

clue.text: Scot heading for rope in bottom of boat and fish

parts.note: Mac is a common nickname for a Scotsman

indicators.note: the letter is put into the boat's base

parts.note: the keel runs along the bottom of a boat

indicators.note: the first letter of the word rope

explanation.surface: A Scot puts rope in the boat's bottom along with a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Mackerel is a common oily sea fish.
